question: Does the bounded Chrome state signature distinguish visible, closed, and reloaded turns in hash-verified flat physical images, without relying on known conversation values?

method.scanner: The unchanged bounded chrome_state_records.scan grammar was applied to one synthetic identity mapping over the fully verified, decompressed physical image in host RAM.
method.read_semantics: A signature or object must occupy physically contiguous bytes; this adapter cannot reassemble a record across nonadjacent physical pages, assign a process, or recover a V8 reference graph.

post_scan_prompt_comparison.scope: Only the prompt was independently compared in this physical scan; the process-mapped trial was scored separately.

screen_only_same_tab_reload_image.separate_existing_result: An answer-only sentence had been found post-hoc in an active renderer in this image; that loose text is not a bounded state object.

interpretation: Two visible-turn images produced complete bounded objects: the still-open tab in the two-tab image and the separate screen-only visible control. The closed-only and screen-only reload images produced zero structural signatures, even though separately tested loose bytes survived. The flat scan does not show that all old text was erased, exclude a physically fragmented object, or assign process ownership without the separate mapped analysis.
